text:
Yanni Gourde is back in Tampa for a second stint, and five games into a return from major hip surgery, the Tampa Bay Times put it plainly: "still a work in progress." One goal, on 0.82 expected goals.

Five games is too few to say much, but the early shape is familiar. Tampa has taken 59% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey's notes on last season make the case for why he's here: opponents got 0.19 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there, 97th percentile among forwards, even as his overall value read around replacement level. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his shots coming off the rush.

What's missing so far is the burst. His EDGE skating speed sits in the 23rd percentile and his hardest shot in the 4th, which may be a 34-year-old finding his legs after surgery. He's a two-time Cup winner with this team who went undrafted and got here through Syracuse; the question for the next month is whether the hip lets him play the game that made him useful in the first place.
